title: Corroborate AGV Active Errors Using AGV Active Error Database Model + Error Code Dictionary + Sort GUID

title: Cancel active exchanges after a manual bag out (purge/close recovery)
summary: After a manual bag out/back out was used because recovery took too long, and the system is back up and running, cancel the active exchanges that were marked by the bag out so operators don’t have to complete the remaining bag out exchange/tote processing.
when_to_use: Use when a manual bag out/back out occurred as a fallback because recovery took too long, and the system is now back up and running; then cancel active exchanges that were marked to exchange by the bag out.
not_for: Do not use if the system is not actually back up and running yet (cancel may not have the intended effect).
Do not use as a generic response to unrelated exchange activity without evidence of a manual bag out/back out event.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute the cancel action via the OptiSweep/WCS API using Apidog on a primary server, then verify that bag-out-marked exchanges are canceled.
safety_notes: Manual bag out/back out is described as a major, labor-intensive event; only proceed with cancel after confirming the system is back up and running.

title: Check OptiSweep API Status and Fault Responses in Apidog
summary: Use Apidog on a primary server to call documented read-oriented OptiSweep / WCS API requests and verify that the API returns an observable response. Do not create new request parameters or build a separate local API project.

safety_notes: Use a documented read-oriented request such as Statuses, FaultStats, or System State for this diagnostic.

Do not submit operational requests such as startup, shutdown, pause, recovery, closeout, purge, or configuration updates as part of the read-only check unless a separately approved procedure directs that action.

title: Check Windows Service State and Logs When the OptiSweep Gateway Is Unavailable
summary: Use Windows Event Viewer / services to inspect the relevant OptiSweep-related service, determine whether it is running or stopped, review available service or Event Viewer logs for crash or inactive-period evidence, and correlate the service state with gateway availability.
when_to_use: Use this Windows Event Viewer / services diagnostic when the OptiSweep gateway is unavailable, does not open, or does not appear to be running, and a stopped service or service crash is suspected.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to restart a service or change service configuration; the supplied evidence supports inspection only.
Do not use this procedure as a complete recovery procedure when the service state or logs do not explain the gateway outage.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only Windows Event Viewer / services inspection and correlates service evidence with gateway availability.
Escalate when the service is stopped or inactive, the gateway remains unavailable, or available logs do not explain the outage.
safety_notes: This is a read-only diagnostic procedure.
Do not perform an unsupported service restart or configuration change based only on this procedure.
access_or_tools_needed: Windows service logs or Event Viewer logs

title: Diagnose Active AGV Errors in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robotics database to inspect current AGV active-error records and identify the affected robot code, error code, description, and SortGuid. When an error is resolved or an AGV is removed, verify that the record is archived to AGVErrorActivityDatabaseModel with available timing fields.
when_to_use: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) Robotics database when an AGV error must be correlated to the affected robot code, error code, error description, and sort during which the error occurred.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify or delete database records.
Do not use this procedure as a physical AGV recovery or production-stop procedure.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only SSMS inspection of the Robotics database.
Escalate when the active record cannot be correlated to the reported AGV condition or lacks expected identifying fields.
safety_notes: Use read-only inspection only.
Do not modify or delete database records.

access_required: L2_support access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
system_preconditions: An affected AGV or reported AGV error has been identified for correlation.

steps.failure_condition: The error description cannot be correlated to the reported condition, or the active row does not provide enough identifying information.

title: Diagnose Missing Package Dimensions in the Ignition Lane Activity Model
summary: Use the live Ignition gateway's Lane Activity Model in the Sorter Sweeper Database view to determine whether incomplete package dimensions are associated with Scan Data 2, Induct, or SortConf records and whether the condition is concentrated on an auto-induct source. Inspect package identifiers, tracking numbers, dimensional fields, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData.
when_to_use: Use this live Ignition gateway diagnostic when sorter totes are overfilling or package data appears incomplete and support needs to determine whether default dimensions were used, which dimensional attribute is missing, and whether the condition is associated with a particular auto-induct source.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to change default dimensions, package classification, or database values.
Do not use this procedure to direct or perform dimensioner reboot or other physical equipment remediation.
Do not treat the observed MissingDimensionData rate as a universal pass/fail threshold; the source provides examples but no universal threshold.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the live Ignition gateway inspection and interprets the Lane Activity Model records.
The site support contact or site operator provides the affected package, tracking number, operational symptoms, and any required physical equipment confirmation.
No role changes database values or package-dimension defaults as part of this diagnostic.
safety_notes: This is an inspection-only diagnostic. Do not modify default dimensions, package classification, or database values.
If physical dimensioner remediation is being considered, communicate the observed data condition to the site support contact rather than directing the physical action from this procedure.
access_or_tools_needed: Package ID or tracking number for the affected parcels

access_required: L2_support access to the Ignition gateway and the Sorter Sweeper Database view
system_preconditions: Recent lane activity records are available for inspection.
The affected package ID, package UID, or tracking number is available when record-level correlation is required.

visual_references.description: Ignition Lane Activity Model view showing message, package identifier, tracking number, dimensional fields, cube, package classification, and MissingDimensionData-related columns.
Lane activity records filtered to sort-confirmation data, illustrating repeated missing width, height, and weight values and correlation with an auto-induct source.
Lane Activity Model records used to inspect missing dimension data during a reported dimensioner-data interruption.

steps.title: Inspect package and dimensional fields in the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Identify the package record and determine which dimensional values are present or missing.
steps.instruction: For the affected records in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model, inspect PackageLid or package ID, PackageUID where displayed, TrackingNumber, Length, Width, Height, Weight, Cube, PackageClassification, and MissingDimensionData.
steps.expected_result: The records show observable package identifiers and dimensional values, including any NULL or missing Length, Width, Height, or Weight values and the associated Cube value.

steps.title: Interpret MissingDimensionData against the live dimensions
steps.purpose: Determine whether default dimensions were applied and identify the missing dimensional attribute.
steps.instruction: Compare MissingDimensionData with Length, Width, Height, Weight, and Cube for each affected record in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model. Treat MissingDimensionData=true as an indication that default dimensional values were used, then identify which dimensional field is NULL or otherwise missing.
steps.expected_result: The comparison identifies whether defaults were used and shows the missing attribute, such as Weight, Width, or Height, while retaining the observed Cube value.
steps.healthy_condition: MissingDimensionData is not true for the reviewed records, or any true value is explainable by the specific missing attribute shown in the dimensional fields.
steps.failure_condition: MissingDimensionData=true is present across affected records and the associated dimensional fields show missing values that can account for incomplete package data or overfilling.

actions.label: Compare missing-data flag
actions.exact_action: Compare the MissingDimensionData value with the dimensional fields and identify NULL or missing dimensional values.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if MissingDimensionData is true across a substantial set of recent records, especially when the records coincide with tote overfilling.
Do not assign a universal percentage threshold; the source does not define one.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: MissingDimensionData becomes true when default dimensions are used. Width and height commonly arrive together, while length is usually present but not always; an example identifies a high rate of missing weight data.

steps.title: Correlate missing dimensions with the auto-induct source
steps.purpose: Determine whether the missing-dimension condition is concentrated on one auto-induct source.
steps.instruction: Use the package ID or related induct identifier in the Ignition gateway Lane Activity Model to compare affected records from the same source, such as Auto Induct 1 or Auto Induct 2. Review the associated Message and dimensional fields for the grouped records.
steps.expected_result: The records show whether MissingDimensionData and the missing dimensional attribute are concentrated on one auto-induct source.
steps.healthy_condition: The affected records can be associated with an auto-induct source and do not show a source-specific pattern of missing dimensions.
steps.failure_condition: Records from one auto-induct source consistently show MissingDimensionData=true or repeated missing dimensional fields, such as missing width, height, or weight.

title: Diagnose AGV Location Dwell in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Robotics Database to inspect active and completed AGV dwell records. Identify the AGV, station, SortGuid, and elapsed-time evidence associated with a tracked location dwell.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when investigating AGV waiting, idle time, or possible bottlenecks at a tracked hospital, tipper, or other station. Inspect the WCS / Helix Robotics Database in SSMS to determine whether the dwell is currently active or has been archived.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify DwellTracking settings or database records.
Do not use dwell records to identify a specific worker or tipper operator; the available evidence does not provide personnel cycling information.
Do not use this procedure as a complete throughput investigation or to optimize one location without considering system-level throughput.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the read-only SSMS inspection of the WCS / Helix Robotics Database and interpret the active or completed dwell fields.
Review or assist when expected dwell evidence is missing or the displayed identifying or timing fields are insufficient for interpretation.

safety_notes: This is a read-only database diagnostic. Do not modify DwellTracking settings or database records.
Treat dwell information as system-throughput evidence. A dwell interval at one location may not represent the effect on overall system throughput.

access_required: L2 or L3 access to the WCS / Helix Robotics Database through SSMS
system_preconditions: The relevant station is configured for DwellTracking when an active dwell is expected.

visual_references.description: Robotics Database view showing LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity fields, including AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.

steps.title: Open the Robotics Database in SSMS
steps.purpose: Access the WCS / Helix Robotics Database tables used to identify active and completed location dwell.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), select the Robotics Database and locate the LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity tables.
steps.expected_result: The Robotics Database is selected and the two named dwell tables are available for read-only inspection.
steps.healthy_condition: SSMS provides access to the Robotics Database and the dwell tables can be inspected without changing data.
steps.failure_condition: The Robotics Database or either named dwell table is unavailable, or the access level would require modification of database records.

actions.label: Select Robotics Database
actions.exact_action: Open SSMS and select the Robotics Database.

actions.label: Locate dwell tables
actions.exact_action: Locate LocationActiveDwellModel and LocationDwellActivity.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L3_support if the Robotics Database or named dwell tables cannot be accessed.

steps.title: Inspect active dwell records
steps.purpose: Determine whether an AGV is currently dwelling at a station configured for DwellTracking.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect LocationActiveDwellModel for active rows at locations marked for DwellTracking. Review the AgvName, Station, and SortGuid fields.
steps.expected_result: An active dwell row, when present, identifies the AGV in AgvName, the tracked location in Station, and the associated sort in SortGuid.
steps.healthy_condition: The active row contains the displayed identifying fields: AgvName, Station, and SortGuid.
steps.failure_condition: A station expected to use DwellTracking has no active row, or the active row lacks AgvName, Station, or SortGuid needed for interpretation.

actions.label: Inspect active dwell model
actions.exact_action: Inspect LocationActiveDwellModel for locations marked for DwellTracking.

actions.label: Review active identifiers
actions.exact_action: Check AgvName, Station, and SortGuid for the active dwell record.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 engineering if a station expected to use DwellTracking has no corresponding active dwell evidence.
Escalate if the active record lacks the displayed identifying fields needed for interpretation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: LocationActiveDwellModel displays active dwells at locations marked for DwellTracking with AgvName, Station, and SortGuid.

steps.title: Correlate the active row with the reported AGV station
steps.purpose: Check whether the active database association agrees with available live AGV location evidence.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the LocationActiveDwellModel Station and AgvName values with the AGV's current location or reported station when that evidence is available through the live support investigation.
steps.expected_result: The active database row associates the AGV named in AgvName with the station named in Station for the current dwell.
steps.healthy_condition: The available AGV location evidence is consistent with the active row's AgvName and Station.
steps.failure_condition: The available AGV location evidence conflicts with the active row, or no current-location evidence is available to perform the comparison.

actions.label: Compare AGV and station
actions.exact_action: Compare the active row's AgvName and Station with the AGV's current location or reported station when available.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate for further review if available live AGV location evidence conflicts with the active database row.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: An active dwell is collected when the AGV gets to a station configured for dwell tracking.

steps.title: Inspect the archived dwell activity
steps.purpose: Recover the completed dwell interval after the AGV has left the tracked location.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect LocationDwellActivity for the AGV and station of interest. Review AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.
steps.expected_result: A completed activity row contains the AGV, station, and sort identifiers together with Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time. A displayed interval may appear in a format such as 00:00:04.9803282.

steps.failure_condition: No completed activity is present after the AGV leaves the tracked location, or the row lacks AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, or Total Time.

actions.exact_action: Check AgvName, Station, SortGuid, Start Time, Finish Time, and Total Time.

steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), use the LocationDwellActivity Station and Total Time values to record the observed dwell interval and determine whether the live record names a hospital, tipper, or another tracked location.
steps.expected_result: The recorded result identifies the station named in Station and the elapsed interval shown in Total Time, such as 00:00:04.9803282.
steps.healthy_condition: The station and Total Time are visible and can be associated with the AGV and SortGuid in the same completed record.
steps.failure_condition: The station or Total Time is absent, or the record cannot be associated with an AGV and SortGuid.

actions.exact_action: Use the displayed Total Time and station values to record the observed dwell interval.

actions.exact_action: Identify whether the live Station value names a hospital, tipper, or other tracked location.

failure_conditions: A station expected to use DwellTracking has no active or completed dwell evidence.

A completed record lacks Start Time, Finish Time, or Total Time.

escalation_guidance: Escalate to L2/L3 engineering when expected active or completed dwell evidence is missing.

Use the dwell result as system-throughput evidence and avoid attributing a tipper interval to a specific worker.
Do not modify DwellTracking or database records during this diagnostic.

title: Diagnose Sorter Location and Queue Mapping in the Robotics Database
summary: Use read-only SSMS access to the WCS / Helix Robotics database to verify sorted-location rows, associated queue locations, sorter-side associations, and sorter-entry sequence when investigating sorter mapping behavior.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic on the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) when support needs to verify sorter-side, sorted-location, queue-location, or sorter-entry sequence configuration associated with an observed sorter mapping issue.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify Robotics database configuration.
Do not use this procedure as a substitute for confirming the physical sorter layout when the database-to-floor relationship is unknown.
Do not use this procedure to diagnose unrelated AGV errors, robot commands, charging, or dwell behavior.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only inspection in SSMS.
L3_support reviews or assists with escalation when a required row, queue association, sorter-side value, or sequence does not match the observed configuration.
safety_notes: Keep the SSMS check read-only.
Do not modify database configuration as part of this procedure.

access_required: L2 or L3 access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
system_preconditions: The affected sorter side, sorted location, or queue location has been identified well enough to select the relevant Robotics database rows.
external_references: Observed sorter configuration or queue order supplied by the site or incident investigation

steps.title: Inspect sorted-location and queue-location rows

Inspect the sorted-location identifier and its associated queue-location identifier; where present, use the model fields SorterId, StagingId, and QueueId to distinguish the sorter location, staging location, and queue location.
steps.expected_result: The affected sorted locations and their associated queue locations are visible as rows that can be compared with the observed sorter configuration.
steps.healthy_condition: Each required sorted location has a corresponding queue-location association, and the association represents the location behind the sorted location where an empty-tote AGV stages for an exchange.
steps.failure_condition: A required sorted-location row is missing, the QueueId association is absent, or the row does not identify the expected queue location.

actions.label: Review location associations
actions.exact_action: Review rows for the sorted locations and the associated queue locations behind those sorted locations.

stop_or_escalate_if: The required location row is missing.
The queue-location association is absent.
The database row cannot be related to the affected sorter location.

Robotics database view and explanation of sorted locations, respective queue locations, sorter-side association, and sequence.

steps.title: Check sorter-side and entrance-queue sequence
steps.purpose: Determine whether the database maps each location to the intended sorter side and preserves the expected order from the sorter entrance queue.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), inspect the sorter-side association and Sequence for each relevant row. Compare the recorded sequence with the observed sorter entrance queue order. Sequence values are used to order the locations from the sorter entrance queue; the supplied model reference describes sequence values 1–4 as starting at that entrance queue.
steps.expected_result: Each relevant location has a sorter-side association and a sequence that can be compared to its expected position from the sorter entrance queue.
steps.healthy_condition: The sorter-side value identifies the intended side, and the sequence progresses consistently with the observed entrance-queue order.
steps.failure_condition: A sorter-side value is missing or unexpected, sequence values do not correspond to the entrance-queue order, or the mapping points to a different location than the observed configuration.

actions.exact_action: Check the sorter-side association for each location.

actions.label: Compare sequence order
actions.exact_action: Compare the recorded sequence with the sorter entrance queue order.

The sequence cannot be reconciled with the sorter entrance queue order.
The observed configuration is insufficient to determine whether the database mapping is correct.

steps.title: Confirm complete mapping for the affected sorter side
steps.purpose: Conclude whether the required sorted locations, queue locations, sorter-side associations, and sequence values form a consistent mapping.
steps.instruction: In the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), verify that all locations and queue associations needed for the affected sorter side are present and that their sorter-side and Sequence values remain consistent with the observed sorter entrance queue order. Keep the inspection read-only.
steps.expected_result: The affected sorter side has a complete, internally consistent set of sorted-location and queue-location mappings.
steps.healthy_condition: All required rows are present; each sorted location has its expected queue location; sorter-side associations match the affected side; and sequence values identify the expected entrance-queue order.
steps.failure_condition: Any required row or queue association is missing, or the sorter-side and sequence values conflict with the observed configuration.

actions.exact_action: Verify that the locations and queue associations needed for the affected sorter side are present and have a consistent sequence.

stop_or_escalate_if: The required location row is missing.
The queue-location association is absent.
Sorter-side or sequence values do not correspond to the observed configuration.
A database change would be needed to make the mapping consistent.

Preserve the read-only findings, including the affected location, queue association, sorter-side value, and sequence value, for escalation.

title: Verify UPS chat message flow for sorter induction, destination enable/close, and label print triggers
summary: Verify that the live Sorter Sweeper ↔ UPS chat message sequence is occurring for a tote/parcel: tote inducted + destination enabled, scan-derived dimensions/load category collection, sort confirmation, optional hot bin/hop-in closeout triggering exchange, destination close before exchange, and print label message to the printer at the tipper stage.
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm that the UPS-facing chat message sequence described for the Sorter Sweeper module is present and progressing for totes/parcels (induction → destination enable → scan data → sort confirmation → hot bin/hop-in exchange → destination close → print label).
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute live checks using the OptiSweep/WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API) and, if needed, corroborate via Ignition gateway tag surfaces.
access_or_tools_needed: Live tote/parcel identifiers to correlate message evidence

access_required: Apidog / WCS API client access (primary server)
system_preconditions: Sorter Sweeper ↔ UPS chat messaging is expected to be active for the tote/parcel being investigated.

visual_references.description: Frame showing the UPS chat message sequence: tote inducted + destination enabled; scan data (dimensions/load category); sort sent and sort confirmation; hot bin/hop-in closeout triggers exchange; destination close before exchange; print label message to printer.

steps.failure_condition: API queries fail (e.g., no response/timeout) such that message evidence cannot be retrieved.

actions.exact_action: Open the live OptiSweep/WCS API client surface (Apidog / WCS API).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the API cannot be queried reliably, escalate for deeper API responsiveness investigation (wcs_api_responsiveness).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: XLE COM manages communication between the Sorter Sweeper module and the UPS chat server; Sorter Sweeper sends tote inducted + destination enabled to the chat and listens for scan data; sort is sent from XLE to the chat; sort confirmation is sent from the sorter onto the chat; destination close is sent before exchange; print label message is sent to the printer.

steps.title: Identify the live API requests/endpoints that correspond to each UPS chat message type in the sequence
steps.purpose: Map the described UPS chat message sequence to concrete live API queries so you can verify ordered presence for the same tote/parcel.
steps.instruction: Using the live OptiSweep/WCS API client, identify the API requests/endpoints that provide evidence for: tote inducted message, destination enabled message, scan-derived dimensions/load category, sort confirmation, hot bin/hop-in message (if applicable), destination close message, and print label message to the printer.
steps.expected_result: You have a set of live API queries that can return evidence records for each message type listed above.
steps.healthy_condition: Each message type can be retrieved as a distinct evidence record set that can be correlated by tote/parcel identifier.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate any live API evidence for one or more required message types (tote inducted, destination enabled, sort confirmation, destination close, print label).

actions.label: Map message types to API evidence
actions.exact_action: Identify the live API endpoints/requests that correspond to the UPS chat message exchanges described in the segment (tote inducted message, destination enabled message, sort confirmation, hot bin message/hop-in message, destination close message, print label message).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the API evidence mapping cannot be established for required message types, stop and escalate for SME mapping of message types to live API fields/endpoints.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Sequence described: send tote inducted + destination enabled to chat; listen for scan data from scan tunnel; collect dimensions and load category; sort sent from XLE to chat; collect possible destinations; sort confirmation sent from sorter onto chat; UPS can trigger hot bin close out via hot bin message for totes that are hot bin and exchange immediately; send destination close message onto chat before exchange; at tipper send print label message to printer so it can print a label provided by XLE.

steps.title: Verify tote inducted + destination enabled evidence for the same tote/parcel
steps.purpose: Confirm the induction stage of the UPS chat sequence is present and not stuck before destination enable.
steps.instruction: For a tote/parcel currently in process, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for both: (1) tote inducted message and (2) destination enabled message. Correlate both evidence records to the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.expected_result: Both tote inducted and destination enabled evidence records are present for the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.healthy_condition: The two evidence records are present together for the same tote/parcel and do not indicate the process is stuck before destination enable.
steps.failure_condition: Tote inducted exists but destination enabled is missing for the same tote/parcel, or the evidence indicates the sequence is stuck earlier.

actions.label: Query induction evidence
actions.exact_action: Query the API for evidence that a tote inducted message and a destination enabled message were sent/received for that tote.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if tote inducted is present but destination enabled is missing for the same tote/parcel.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “So the tote arrives at the sorter, we send a tote inducted message and a destination enabled message to the chat.”

steps.title: Verify scan-derived dimensions and load category evidence
steps.purpose: Confirm the scan tunnel data collection stage is occurring and populating the parcel attributes used downstream.
steps.instruction: For the same tote/parcel context, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for scan-derived parcel dimensions and load category fields that are described as coming from the scan tunnel onto the chat.
steps.expected_result: Dimensions and load category fields are populated for the parcel/tote context.
steps.healthy_condition: Dimension and load category values are present (not null/empty) for the same tote/parcel identifier that has induction evidence.
steps.failure_condition: Scan-derived dimensions and/or load category are missing or not populated for the tote/parcel in process.

actions.label: Query scan data evidence
actions.exact_action: Query for scan/parcel data collection evidence (dimensions and load category) that is described as coming from the scan tunnel onto the chat.

stop_or_escalate_if: If scan-derived dimensions/load category are missing while induction evidence exists, escalate for deeper module-level investigation (Sorter Sweeper vs XLE COM vs OPC COM).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “We listen to scan data too, which is from the scan tunnel. We collect the dimensions of the parcel and the load category.”
Example evidence view includes columns for TrackingNumber and Length/Width/Height/Weight (dimension fields) alongside sort confirmation filtering.

steps.title: Verify sort confirmation evidence includes final destination
steps.purpose: Confirm the sort stage is completed and that the parcel has a final destination in the confirmation evidence.

steps.expected_result: A sort confirmation evidence record exists for the tote/parcel and includes a final destination.
steps.healthy_condition: Sort confirmation evidence is present and shows a final destination value for the same tote/parcel identifier.
steps.failure_condition: Sort confirmation evidence is missing, or it exists without a final destination value.

actions.label: Query sort confirmation
actions.exact_action: Query for sort confirmation evidence that sort was sent from XLE onto the chat and that a sort confirmation was sent from the sorter onto the chat.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if sort confirmation evidence is missing for the tote/parcel.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Sort is sent from XLE so it's UPS version of WCS on to the chat… We collect the possible destinations for each parcel and then we get a sort confirmation as sent from the sorter onto the chat.”

steps.title: Verify hot bin closeout / hop-in exchange evidence (when expected)
steps.purpose: Confirm the hot bin/hop-in closeout path triggers an exchange immediately when UPS sends the hot bin message.
steps.instruction: If the tote(s) are expected to be hop-in/hot-bin, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for hot bin message/hop-in message records for those totes. Confirm that the exchange-related state advances immediately after the hot bin/hop-in evidence.
steps.expected_result: Hot bin/hop-in evidence exists for the tote(s) and exchange-related state advances immediately after.
steps.healthy_condition: For hop-in/hot-bin totes, hot bin/hop-in evidence is present and exchange advancement is observable in the evidence timeline for the same tote(s).
steps.failure_condition: Hot bin/hop-in evidence is missing when expected, or exchange advancement does not occur immediately after hot bin/hop-in evidence.

actions.label: Query hot bin/hop-in evidence
actions.exact_action: Query for a hot bin message/hop-in message for totes that are hop in and confirm an exchange is triggered immediately.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if hot bin/hop-in evidence is missing for totes that are expected to be hop-in.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “UPS can trigger a hop in close out by sending us a hop in message for all totes that are hop in and we do an exchange immediately.”

steps.title: Verify destination close message exists before exchange advancement
steps.purpose: Confirm the destination close stage is sent before the exchange occurs.
steps.instruction: Before the exchange-related state advances for the tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for a destination close message being sent onto the chat. Correlate it to the destination tied to the tote.
steps.expected_result: A destination close message evidence record exists for the destination tied to the tote before exchange-related state advances.
steps.healthy_condition: Destination close evidence is present and occurs earlier in the evidence timeline than exchange advancement for the same tote/parcel.
steps.failure_condition: Destination close message is missing, or exchange advancement occurs without destination close evidence preceding it.

actions.label: Query destination close evidence
actions.exact_action: Before an exchange, query for a destination close message being sent onto the chat.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if destination close message is missing before the exchange-related state advances.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “And then when the totes is ready to leave… we send the destination close message onto the chat before we do an exchange.”

steps.title: Verify print label message is sent at the tipper stage
steps.purpose: Confirm the final stage: label print trigger message is sent to the printer with the label provided by XLE.
steps.instruction: At the tipper stage for the tote/parcel, query the live OptiSweep/WCS API evidence for a print label message being sent to the printer. Confirm it is associated with the label provided by XLE (e.g., label payload/identifier present).
steps.expected_result: A print label message evidence record exists and is associated with the label provided by XLE (label payload/identifier present).
steps.healthy_condition: Print label evidence is present for the tote/parcel at the tipper stage and includes an associated label identifier/payload.
steps.failure_condition: Print label message evidence is missing at the tipper stage.

actions.label: Query print label evidence
actions.exact_action: At the tipper stage, query for a print label message being sent to the printer.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if print label message evidence is missing at the tipper stage.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “And then at the tipper, we send a print label message to the printer so it can print a label provided by the XLE.”

steps.title: Stop and escalate on missing/out-of-order message evidence
steps.purpose: Ensure rapid escalation when the required message sequence is incomplete or out of order for the same tote/parcel.
steps.instruction: If any required message evidence is missing or out of order for the same tote/parcel (tote inducted present but destination enabled missing; sort confirmation missing; destination close missing before exchange; print label missing at tipper), stop further checks and escalate for deeper module-level investigation.
steps.expected_result: A clear escalation decision is made based on which message evidence is missing/out of order.
steps.healthy_condition: All required message evidence is present in the expected order for the tote/parcel under investigation.
steps.failure_condition: Any required evidence is missing or the order is violated for the same tote/parcel.

actions.label: Escalate based on evidence gap
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if any required message evidence is missing (e.g., tote inducted present but destination enabled missing; sort confirmation missing; destination close missing before exchange; print label message missing at tipper).

sort confirmation missing
destination close missing before exchange
print label message missing at tipper
only one side present (e.g., scan data present but sort confirmation missing)

At the tipper stage, print label message evidence exists and is associated with the label provided by XLE.

Hot bin/hop-in evidence missing when tote(s) are expected to be hop-in.
Destination close missing before exchange advancement.
Print label message missing at the tipper stage.

title: Check AGV State, Command Vitals, and Errors in the OptiSweep WCS API

when_to_use: Use this Apidog / OptiSweep WCS API diagnostic when support needs to verify an AGV's live state, current command information, vitals, network identity, or AGV and system error indications.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to remove, recover, pause, resume, or execute an AGV command.

errorAlert is true.

title: Check Ignition Gateway Performance Metrics
summary: An L2 support user can open the live Ignition gateway performance page in a web browser and review CPU, memory, connection, response-time, slow-response, garbage-collector, and tuning-script indicators for evidence of gateway health or degradation.
when_to_use: Use this Ignition gateway diagnostic procedure when gateway health, performance degradation, an unplanned restart, or related OPC and application symptoms require live evidence from the Ignition Gateway performance page.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for a physical E-stop, LOTO, or physical AGV recovery.
Do not infer numeric healthy thresholds for CPU, memory, response time, garbage collectors, or other indicators from this procedure.

title: Diagnose Ignition Gateway Performance Using the Performance Page
summary: Use the Ignition gateway performance page in a web browser to review Memory Trend, CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events while investigating an OptiSweep system issue. The memory chart can provide evidence of a spike followed by a drop to 0, but the Gateway chart alone does not establish the underlying application fault.
when_to_use: Use the Ignition gateway performance page when investigating an OptiSweep system issue and Gateway-level memory, response, or slow-response behavior needs to be checked.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a Perspective diagnostic; the source distinguishes the Ignition gateway from Perspective.
Do not treat the Gateway performance chart alone as proof of the underlying application fault or as the sole explanation for a reported system symptom.
Do not use this procedure as a service restart procedure; the supplied evidence does not provide a complete named service restart workflow.

L2_support correlates the displayed evidence with the reported system behavior and escalates when the page cannot be opened or the evidence does not explain the symptom.
safety_notes: This is an observation-only diagnostic procedure based on the supplied evidence; no production stop or physical intervention is specified.
A memory spike followed by a drop to 0 is an indicator associated with a crash, not proof of the underlying application cause.

when_to_use: Use the live Ignition gateway System Performance page when troubleshooting suspected gateway performance, connectivity, runtime, or response problems and a current view of gateway resource and subsystem indicators is needed.

title: Diagnose AGV Robot Command State in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) in read-only mode to trace an AGV command through the Robotics Database RobotCommandDatabaseModel active-command table and Robot Command Activity history. Review command identity, status, robot, container, station, location, parameters, and lifecycle timing fields to determine whether the command was sent, started, completed, errored, or cancelled.
when_to_use: Use this diagnostic on the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) when support needs to verify the lifecycle of an AGV command requested by the Robotics module, including whether an active command is Sent or InProgress, whether it has been archived, or whether it has an errored or cancelled status.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify database records, resubmit commands, remove or recover an AGV, restart services, or issue other command changes.
Do not use this procedure as a replacement for physical AGV recovery or safety actions.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) inspection.
L3_support may review the database interpretation and assist with escalation when the command is errored, cancelled, stuck, or missing.
safety_notes: This is a read-only diagnostic. Do not modify database records or issue command changes.
An errored or cancelled command requires escalation to L2/L3 support rather than corrective database edits.

steps.purpose: Determine whether the command was sent, progressed to execution, or remains active without expected progression.

when_to_use: Use this diagnostic when support needs to verify the live tipper configuration used by the system, including the station-to-tipper association, printer configuration, location association, or current Tipper Status in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS).
not_for: Changing printer, location, station, or tipper-status configuration.
Operating or recovering a tipper through the Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU.
Replacing a live equipment fault investigation with configuration inspection alone.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the read-only inspection in the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and record the observed Tipper model values.
Review or assist with inconsistent, missing, Not Ready, or Disabled Tipper model records.

safety_notes: Use read-only inspection only. This procedure does not authorize changing printer, location, station, or status configuration.
A Not Ready or Disabled value is an observed configuration/status condition and requires escalation rather than an in-procedure change.

access_required: L2/L3 access to the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only surface.
system_preconditions: The relevant operator station or tipper must be identified before inspecting the Tipper model record.
external_references: Tipper station reference: standard and GLD operator stations are described as having two tippers per station.

steps.healthy_condition: A Tipper model record is present for the identified station.
steps.failure_condition: The relevant Tipper model record cannot be located or is missing.

actions.exact_action: Open the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) read-only view of the Sorter Sweeper Database and locate the Tipper model records for the relevant operator station.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to L2/L3 support if the relevant Tipper model record is missing.

steps.title: Verify Tipper ID and station association

steps.failure_condition: The Tipper ID is absent, the station association is inconsistent, or the left/right representation cannot be reconciled with the station.

actions.exact_action: Check the Tipper ID and station association, including the documented left/right representation used for the station.

steps.title: Check printer name and printer IP

steps.healthy_condition: Printer Name and printer IP are present when the tipper is expected to use a configured printer.
steps.failure_condition: Printer information is absent when a printer is required, or the displayed printer information does not match the expected tipper configuration.

actions.exact_action: Check the Printer Name and associated printer IP used for label directives, when a printer is configured for the tipper.

steps.title: Verify the Location ID

steps.expected_result: The Tipper model contains a Location ID that can be compared with the expected station location.
steps.healthy_condition: The Location ID is present and matches the expected station location.
steps.failure_condition: The Location ID is absent or does not match the expected station location.

title: Validate Sorter Location Records and Lane Status in SSMS
summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) in read-only mode to inspect the SorterSweeper Location Model, verify station and location mappings, and interpret LaneStatus for a selected sorter, tipper, hospital, or induction location.
when_to_use: Use this read-only WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) diagnostic when support must validate a SorterSweeper location record, station or cell-code mapping, location category, lane status, or related KeepClose and TipperSelect configuration.
not_for: Do not use this procedure to modify database rows or configuration values.
Do not use this procedure as a physical sorter, AGV, hospital, or tipper recovery procedure.
Do not treat a nullable LoadCategory or AGV-related field as a fault solely because its value is NULL.
Do not use this procedure to infer an undocumented LaneStatus value or an unverified station mapping.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the read-only inspection in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS), compare the selected location fields, and document the observed mapping and LaneStatus.
Review or investigate missing rows, mapping mismatches, undocumented statuses, or locations that remain Not tracking when expected to participate in sorter operation.

safety_notes: This is a read-only diagnostic. Do not update database or configuration values as part of this procedure.
LaneStatus interpretation is observational: Active is open for use, Bypassed is closed, and Not tracking is excluded from use until it becomes Active or Bypassed.
access_or_tools_needed: Read-only access to the WCS / Helix SorterSweeper database
SorterSweeper Location Model or corresponding location records

access_required: L2_support or L3_support access to WCS / Helix DB (SSMS)

title: Use OptiSweep/WCS API actions to reopen all chutes and cancel closeout exchanges
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API) to (1) reopen any previously closed shoots/chutes and (2) cancel closeout exchanges that are not currently in progress. This is intended for recovery after a customer manual bag-out/closeout where the sort was not cycled.
when_to_use: When a customer did a manual bag out/closeout and the system needs to start up again without cycling the sort.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the OptiSweep / WCS API client actions and verify each call returns a successful result before stopping.
access_or_tools_needed: Apidog / WCS API client (or equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client)

access_required: Access to the OptiSweep / WCS API client (Apidog / WCS API) on the primary servers
system_preconditions: The system is in a state where chutes/shoots may be closed and closeout exchanges may exist but are not in progress.

visual_references.description: System API actions list showing: Open All Chutes (opens all closed shoots) and Cancel close out (cancels closeout exchanges that are not in progress).

steps.title: Locate OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and check Running vs Stopped
steps.purpose: Determine whether the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Running or Stopped during the suspected silent/crash window.
steps.instruction: In the Services list, locate the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) (the segment notes there are about 10 services) and check the Status column for Running vs Stopped.
steps.expected_result: You identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and observe their Status as Running or Stopped.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Running during normal operation.
steps.failure_condition: The OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Stopped, or you observe restart behavior consistent with the suspected crash/restart period.

actions.label: Find relevant services and read Status
actions.exact_action: In the Services list, locate the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and check the Status column for Running vs Stopped.

stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “the service must stop” and “the log will be silent” and “how will someone support… know that service is just gone… It’s a Windows… you check the service services… there are 10 services.”

steps.title: Interpret Stopped/restarting service state as evidence consistent with the silent crash window
steps.purpose: Use the service state as the observable indicator when logs are silent, matching the segment’s described behavior during crash periods.
steps.instruction: If the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Stopped (or show restart behavior), treat that as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period during the suspected crash window.
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion matches the observed Status: Stopped/restarting supports the suspected crash/restart period; Running supports normal operation.
steps.healthy_condition: During normal operation, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Running.
steps.failure_condition: During the suspected crash window, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Stopped or restarting.

actions.label: Confirm evidence from service state
actions.exact_action: If the service is Stopped (or repeatedly restarting), treat this as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period.

stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot map which of the ~10 services corresponds to the affected component

steps.title: Stop and escalate when service identification/status is unclear
steps.purpose: Ensure you do not proceed with an unsupported conclusion when the relevant service(s) cannot be identified or the status evidence is not clear.
steps.instruction: If you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list, or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status, stop and escalate.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated with the evidence that the relevant service(s) could not be identified or status was unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant service(s) are identifiable and show clear Running/Stopped status.
steps.failure_condition: Service identification is ambiguous or the Services view does not provide clear Running/Stopped status.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.

stop_or_escalate_if: Cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) among the ~10 services

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “there are 10 services” and the segment’s stated challenge is knowing the service is gone when logs are silent by checking Windows Services.

success_criteria: You can identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) in the Windows Services MMC and observe clear Status values (Running vs Stopped).
During the suspected crash window, the observed service state (Stopped/restarting) aligns with the segment’s described “service must stop” / “logs may be silent” behavior.
healthy_conditions: OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Running in the Windows Services MMC during normal operation.
failure_conditions: OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Stopped during the suspected crash window.
OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show restart behavior consistent with an unplanned crash/restart period.
Relevant service(s) cannot be identified among the ~10 services, or Running/Stopped status is unclear.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if you cannot map which of the ~10 services corresponds to the affected component or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.
